title: Railway Changelog #0309: Free VMs without an account
brief: Railway Changelog #0309 opens free Linux VMs with no account: `ssh railway.new` gets a 2 vCPU/2 GB box with coding agents preinstalled, 60 minutes to build and 24 hours to claim it before deletion. The same edition adds request tracing in Priority Boarding (edge-to-database waterfalls with no code changes) and OpenCode on Cloud Agents for persistent agent VMs.

title: Orca
brief: A free, open-source Agent Development Environment (ADE): run Claude Code, Codex, Gemini, Cursor CLI, and other CLI agents in parallel across isolated git worktrees, with a Ghostty-class terminal, in-app diff review, embedded browser, and SSH dev built in. Bring your own subscriptions — agents run side by side without interfering.

title: heddlework
brief: A native, harness-neutral workspace for agent sessions: task graphs, diffs, and durable work across coding agents — Pi first, Codex and Claude next. Very early (~12 stars); expect rough edges.
caveat: Very early (~12 stars); expect rough edges.

title: gpui-kit
brief: Rust GUI components for building cross-platform desktop apps on GPUI (the framework behind Zed). ~14.8k stars — one of the more-starred GPUI component libraries.

title: scenario-labs/skills
brief: Agent skills for Scenario: image, video, audio, texture, 3D, and custom-model workflows over the Scenario MCP, aimed at games, entertainment, and creative verticals. Installs with `npx skills add scenario-labs/skills`; ~450 stars.

title: Detail
brief: A curated gallery of the small UI decisions that make products feel considered — smarter word breaks, corner-morph animations, name-derived placeholders — each shown as a short clip. Curated by Rene Wang; a good reference for stealing micro-interaction ideas.

title: Landbook
brief: A website design inspiration gallery with a large curated collection of landing pages, e-commerce sites, portfolios, and templates, plus boards for saving references. Useful for browsing real-world site design by category.

title: MaxiBestOf
brief: A website design and typography inspiration feed updated every weekday, pairing featured sites with their font stacks (e.g., Geist, Neue Haas Grotesk). A Pro tier adds private collections and HD screenshots.

title: SoulStack
brief: ProxySoul × Empryo: a bundle of skills, agents, an "immune system," and habits for coding agents. Very early (~17 stars); concept-heavy and expect rough edges.
caveat: Very early (~17 stars); concept-heavy and expect rough edges.

title: GLiNER2.5-Decide
brief: Fastino's 340M-parameter open-weight model for schema-defined decision-making: feed it text plus typed questions and get valid answers with probabilities, confidence scores, and constraint-feasibility metadata. Apache 2.0, CPU-capable, strong on routing/triage/guardrail tasks. Benchmark figures are vendor-reported and not independently verified.
caveat: Benchmark figures are vendor-reported and not independently verified.

title: Isoquant
brief: A new PAYGO inference provider launching with GLM-5.3-Flash at $0.07/$0.20 per 1M input/output tokens with automatic prompt caching; drop-in OpenAI-compatible API, no top-up fees. Its published benchmarks claim the lowest latency and highest throughput versus Together, CoreWeave, Baseten, Fireworks, and Z.ai. Pricing and benchmark figures are vendor-reported and not independently verified.
caveat: Pricing and benchmark figures are vendor-reported and not independently verified.

title: kiro-fabric
brief: Kiro Fabric gives Kiro CLI a way to run several tool operations as one checked TypeScript program: Kiro writes the code, Fabric type-checks it and executes it in a fresh QuickJS context, with a repo-navigation layer (Navigator/Fovea) mapping symbols and change impact via ast-grep. Fresh repo (0 stars, MIT); expect rough edges.
caveat: Fresh repo (0 stars, MIT); expect rough edges.

title: Claude Mods (function hooks proposal)
brief: Anthropic's design proposal for Claude Code "Mods" (function hooks): hook into Claude Code with TypeScript functions à la Express/Koa, with side-effect tracking and middleware-style composition — even modifying how components render. Committed to ship in weeks; the first three built-in mods' source listings are linked in the thread.

title: Jev Decision Index
brief: A Hugging Face Space tracking benchmarks and news on the various repros of TypeSafe's Jev — a handy index if you're following the Jev model race.

title: jevgrep
brief: Find code by asking what it does: a CLI (plus an installable agent skill) that uses Jev to judge relevance across folders, files, and declarations, returning relevant files, reading leads, and verbatim source excerpts in one stdout response. Installs with `npm install -g @dzhng/jevgrep`; its own ten-task SWE-bench comparison claims ~30% lower coding-agent cost at equal task success. (~803 stars, MIT.) Cost figures are author-reported and not independently verified.
caveat: Installs with `npm install -g @dzhng/jevgrep`; its own ten-task SWE-bench comparison claims ~30% lower coding-agent cost at equal task success. (~803 stars, MIT.) Cost figures are author-reported and not independently verified.

title: rust-llm-tidy
brief: An opinionated linter aimed at LLM-generated code (Rust, C#, Markdown): fix/reorder/visibility/spacing transforms plus read-only lint checks, runnable per-file, on git-changed files, or in CI via a GitHub Action. The author's personal tooling ("largely written by LLMs"); expect opinionated rules, 0 stars. Apache 2.0.

title: sys-prompt.md
brief: A complete agent-harness system prompt as a gist: JSON tool schemas for edit, glob, grep, question, read, shell, subagent, and write with execution semantics spelled out. Useful reference if you're building or tuning a coding-agent CLI.

title: boxd
brief: Boxd offers "composable computers": persistent KVM dev VMs (2 vCPU, 8 GB RAM, 100 GB disk by default) with live memory forking in under 200ms, snapshots, checkpoints, per-machine HTTPS subdomains, and a CLI/API plus MCP integrations for GitHub, Linear, and Slack — pitched for giving agents root and walking away. Billing is credit-based (about €0.22/h for a default machine per the site; €30 of free credits for new accounts). Pricing figures come from the site and are not independently verified.
caveat: Pricing figures come from the site and are not independently verified.

title: boat
brief: Boat sells cloud sandbox VMs for long-running agents: full VMs (Docker, systemd, databases), an integrated desktop/browser, and a CLI (`boat new`, `boat prompt` runs Claude Code or Codex inside), API, and SDKs, with stop/resume snapshots that pause billing. They claim $0.036/h for 4 vCPU / 8 GB RAM on a $20/mo plan ($20 of sandbox time), with a price table pitching themselves well under E2B, Daytona, Modal, and Vercel Sandbox. These price comparisons are the vendor's own and are not independently verified.
caveat: These price comparisons are the vendor's own and are not independently verified.

title: pi-better-skills
brief: A pi extension that fixes skill ergonomics: skills resolve their bundled files from the skill directory (`$PI_SKILL_DIR` instead of the workspace), each SKILL.md loads whole on first read, and path guidance is injected into the system prompt so authors stop babysitting paths. Installs with `pi install git:github.com/edxeth/pi-better-skills`; ~20 stars, POSIX-only.

title: pi-coralbricks-provider
brief: An npm package (v1.0.19, by monotykamary — also behind pi-tool-repair and pi-mockdeck in this library) that registers CoralBricks as a provider extension for the pi coding agent: GLM 5.3, GLM 5.3 Flash, and DeepSeek V4.1 Flash through the Coral Inference API. It was shared in a support thread asking whether it uses completions or responses endpoints — check the repo README for the current endpoint behavior.

title: The next Git platform on Cloudflare
brief: Cloudflare's blog announces a competition to build the next Git platform on Cloudflare, aimed at an AI-agent era of coding. Read it for the contest details and Cloudflare's take on where agent-driven development tooling is headed.

title: ccdeck
brief: ccdeck is a free, open-source local dashboard for Claude Code and Codex sessions — live session and tool-call views plus cost tracking. Useful if you run multiple agent sessions and want a single pane of glass.

title: hpc-sandbox-benchmarks
brief: A benchmark suite comparing sandbox providers using real high-performance developer and CI/CD workloads, shared as "new benchmarks in town". Check it when choosing between sandbox VM offerings for agents — the results are the author's own and are not independently verified.
caveat: Check it when choosing between sandbox VM offerings for agents — the results are the author's own and are not independently verified.

title: PrimaLabs: MiMo-V2.6-Pro speed benchmark
brief: PrimaLabs benchmarks MiMo-V2.6-Pro on its serverless platform at 407 output tokens/sec (vs Xiaomi's 45 at 10k input tokens), priced at $0.43 in / $0.87 out per million tokens with $0.0036 cache. Speed and pricing figures come from PrimaLabs' post (measured by Artificial Analysis, 24 Sep 2026) and are not independently verified.
caveat: Speed and pricing figures come from PrimaLabs' post (measured by Artificial Analysis, 24 Sep 2026) and are not independently verified.

title: Bitdeer AI Cloud model pricing
brief: Bitdeer AI Cloud's inference pricing page for hosted open-source and enterprise AI models, shared citing GLM-5.3-Flash at $0.075 in / $0.25 out per million tokens ($0.015 cached input) with ~200 tokens/sec. Pricing and throughput figures come from the vendor and are not independently verified.
caveat: Pricing and throughput figures come from the vendor and are not independently verified.

title: Artificial Analysis: GLM-5.3 Flash providers
brief: Artificial Analysis' provider comparison page for GLM-5.3-Flash: which inference providers serve it, at what price and speed. Handy when shopping for the cheapest or fastest GLM-5.3-Flash endpoint.

title: Cua Spaces
brief: A free full-desktop Space for every agent — macOS VMs on machines you own or in your own cloud (Apple silicon Macs for macOS Spaces, Docker or Podman for Linux), connectable to Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Gemini CLI, Cline, Kiro and OpenClaw through the Cua MCP. Its Teleport feature moves an app's whole session (tabs, profile, sign-ins) from your Mac into a Space, with nothing read until you approve and Touch ID gating on sensitive items.

title: Battleships
brief: An agent-readable comparison of sandbox, VM and runtime pricing for AI agents — 366 providers priced through one engine with every figure quoted from the source pricing page, published as llms.txt, JSON files and a Node pricing engine. Built by boat.dev, one of the providers it ranks; the rankings are not independently verified, so take them with a grain of salt.
caveat: Built by boat.dev, one of the providers it ranks; the rankings are not independently verified, so take them with a grain of salt.

title: HostBrr
brief: European VPS and hosting provider (cloud VPS from €3.50/mo, web hosting from €1.25/mo) on AMD EPYC/Threadripper with NVMe storage, a 10Gbps network and included DDoS mitigation; Felix strongly recommends it for non-serious projects, citing best performance-per-dollar in Europe. Felix notes the site's "order" tab is quirky; the performance-per-dollar claim is the sharer's and is not independently verified.
caveat: Felix notes the site's "order" tab is quirky; the performance-per-dollar claim is the sharer's and is not independently verified.

title: HostUp
brief: Swedish VPS provider at ~$10/month + tax for 8 GB RAM, used and vouched for by thelaggingway in reply to ROman. Note: the signup page's bot protection rejected the automated link check, so the URL is posted as-shared and only sharer-verified.

title: TierHive
brief: Hourly-billed NAT VPS hosting aimed at small-VPS needs — deploy instantly, scale dynamically, pay only for hours used, with load balancing and automatic failover included. thelaggingway recommends it for small-VPS needs but hasn't tried it; pricing and feature claims are vendor-reported and not independently verified.

title: HeavenCloud
brief: Indian hosting provider (Mumbai, plus US/Singapore/Germany) for Discord/Telegram bots, Lavalink nodes, game servers and Ryzen VPS — a free 24/7 Discord bot tier with no credit card, paid bot plans from ₹20/mo. The share cites a 99.5% SLA, but the site's FAQ reserves uptime SLAs for paid plans; take the SLA claim with caution.

title: Roll as many dice as the die has sides
brief: A probability paper proving that in the Hog dice game, rolling n dice maximizes the expected turn score for an n-sided die — expectation derived via the law of total expectation, with a full maximum proof and charts. Link-only share with no surrounding context; classifiable from the page itself.
caveat: Link-only share with no surrounding context; classifiable from the page itself.

title: Aoru
brief: Inference provider serving resident open models with zero-log inference behind one OpenAI-compatible endpoint; Plus at $12/month and Pro at $25/month with refilled token balances, plus usage-based PAYG credits from $5. Shared in reply to a 36B tokens/month, $2000/month budget request; pricing and zero-log claims are vendor-reported and not independently verified.
caveat: Shared in reply to a 36B tokens/month, $2000/month budget request; pricing and zero-log claims are vendor-reported and not independently verified.

title: HyperCLI
brief: Flat-rate provider plans for coding agents — Solo $39/month (25M tokens/day), Team $79/month (50M pooled), Pro $149/month (100M pooled) — with OpenAI- and Anthropic-compatible API keys drawing from the same daily pool, capped with throttling instead of overage billing. Shared for the same 36B tokens/month request; 7-day free trial, no card. Plan figures are vendor-reported and not independently verified.
caveat: Plan figures are vendor-reported and not independently verified.

title: Arilo
brief: Flat-rate coding-inference provider with predictable 30-day plans — Coder $0.99, Starter $4.99, Pro $19.99, Hacker $100, up to Small Business $490 — each a prepaid credit allowance against per-token metered pricing, plus an off-peak JSONL batch path at 50% off PAYG. thelaggingway shared it "still to be evaluated", so treat all of this as unevaluated marketing until checked. Conversations are not used for training unless you opt into their Research Program.

title: hyperiux
brief: Hyperiux Vault is a source-first library of interaction effects for React and Next.js — scroll systems, cursor effects, text reveals, page transitions and WebGL scenes that install as editable code in your own repo via the Hyperiux CLI. The free core includes 50+ effects; Pro unlocks all 150+ with new effects added regularly, and code you have installed stays yours even if you cancel.

title: vanta ui
brief: VantaUI is a UI library built from real products — production-grade site templates, app templates, components, blocks and Figma files for Next.js, React and LLM-assisted builds, from @vanta_ui. It doubles as a reference for how world-class products handle UI patterns, copywriting and user flows.

title: bencho
brief: Bencho is a library of interactive React components and micro-interactions — asset swap, heat map, image compare, dynamic island, magnetic select, slide-to-confirm and dozens more — each explorable live and liftable straight into your projects. From @cabralorenzo; a shortcut to polished interactions without building them from scratch.

title: obsidian ui
brief: ObsidianUI is a React and Tailwind CSS component library with an emphasis on motion — featured components and interactive effects you can preview, read the source of, and try directly in your project. From @athrix_codes; a customizable starting point for interfaces where the details matter.

title: beste
brief: Beste UI is a collection of production-ready shadcn/tailwind blocks and components — 2189+ blocks (heroes, pricing, testimonials, error pages) and 1326+ smaller pieces, each self-contained and installed with one shadcn CLI command and no runtime dependency. Free pieces are MIT-licensed for commercial use; Pro blocks need a Beste UI license, though installed code keeps working if the license lapses.

title: Prism Inference
brief: Pay-as-you-go inference with no minimums across serverless, elastic, private and dedicated endpoints, plus batch. Lists per-model rates (GLM-5.3 $1.40/$4.40, Kimi K3 $3/$15 per 1M tokens) and states strict zero data retention — inputs and outputs are never used for training.

title: InferHub
brief: Proxy service that pools AI subscriptions into one API. Shared as "a rly interesting proxy" with per-plan pricing on its site.

title: AIHubMix
brief: Multi-model API with per-model pricing, including a GLM 5.3 coding endpoint. Shared via its GLM 5.3 API pricing page.

title: Surplus Intelligence
brief: OpenAI-compatible inference marketplace that routes each request to the cheapest current offer. Vendor claims ~38% savings via routing; pricing and retention terms weren't independently verified.

title: Kitani
brief: Open inference on independent hardware with a prepaid USD balance — the max request cost is reserved, then settled on completion. API is OpenAI-compatible at api.kitani.ai/v1.

title: Pareto Inference
brief: Pay-per-token inference running on Pareto's own GPUs, including GLM 5.3 Flash. Shared via its pricing page.

title: BytePlus ModelArk
brief: BytePlus's Coding Plan for Claude Code, Cursor, Cline, Kilo Code, Roo Code and OpenCode, covering models like Dola-Seed-2.0-pro, GLM-5.1 and DeepSeek V4. Exact plan prices weren't visible on the promo page.

title: Parasail
brief: Inference provider whose homepage FAQ states explicit zero data retention alongside SLA terms. Surfaced in #providers via a comparisons board post.

title: Inceptron
brief: Inference provider with ISO 27001 certification, GDPR compliance and EU residency. No zero-retention statement was found on its site.

title: Subconscious
brief: An inference platform built for long-running coding agents, using runtime context compression to cut token bills on extended agentic traces; it drops into Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, or any OpenAI-compatible harness, and can also be deployed inside your own cloud. Plans sell as daily token allocations with no per-seat pricing — Base at $100/month for 60M tokens/day, Pro at $500/month for 300M/day, Heavy at $2,000/month for 1.2B/day — plus per-token overflow billing. Its savings and performance claims (2× faster task completion, up to 80% cost reduction) are vendor-reported and not independently verified.
caveat: Its savings and performance claims (2× faster task completion, up to 80% cost reduction) are vendor-reported and not independently verified.

title: FEIHOA
brief: Unlimited AI plans from €6. States prompts and outputs are not used for training, though it may retain data briefly for security, abuse prevention and legal reasons.

title: Crof
brief: Inference provider at crof.ai; public evidence is thin (snippet-based). Third-party substitution allegations seen during research are unverified and not repeated here.
caveat: Third-party substitution allegations seen during research are unverified and not repeated here.

title: Real API Pricing
brief: GitHub repo behind the real-api-pricing comparison of actual inference API prices. Its web app is already in this library's web-apps section; this is the distinct source repo.

title: OpenCode Go
brief: OpenCode's own $10/month subscription bringing its agentic coding experience to OpenCode or any agent, with generous per-model request limits on a curated open-source lineup (Kimi K2.7 Code, MiniMax M3, GLM-5.3-Flash, DeepSeek V4.1 Flash, and others) — limits shown as estimated requests per 5-hour window, with optional top-up credits. Free rotating models appear on a limited-time basis; cancel any time. Usage limits are vendor-stated estimates, and the free rotating models are time-limited.

title: SingularityAPI
brief: A unified AI gateway routing to DeepSeek, Kimi, GLM, and 300+ models through one endpoint, with smart routing by cost, speed, quality, or availability, built-in failover, and usage analytics; it also sells reserved GPU-lane capacity from $0.20/hr for dedicated inference and is currently offering 100% bonus credits on recharges up to $1,000. A forwarded announcement noted DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash going live on the platform. The homepage publishes no per-token price list, and the bonus-credit promo terms are vendor-published.

title: DeepSeek clock
brief: Personal utility page showing DeepSeek's live peak/off-peak status in local time with both models' prices either way. Rates match the official docs.

title: Token Harbor
brief: A pass-based inference API: a free tier with a rotating model allowance, an Agent Pass at $1.99/month ($10 included usage, for always-on agent scripts), an Office Pass at $9.99/month ($35 usage), and a Frontier Pass at $99/month ($180 usage) — each tier unlocking progressively heavier models, with boosted models billing at reduced rates. 'Included usage' is measured at the site's own published per-token prices rather than as a cash wallet balance, so the effective deal is vendor-reported and not independently verified.
caveat: 'Included usage' is measured at the site's own published per-token prices rather than as a cash wallet balance, so the effective deal is vendor-reported and not independently verified.

title: StreamLake
brief: Kuaishou's AI cloud / model-as-a-service platform with API and SDK integration for online inference. Holds ISO 27001/27017/42001 and MLPS Level 3; no explicit zero-retention statement found.

title: CoreWeave
brief: GPU cloud infrastructure company offering serverless inference APIs, dedicated endpoints and GPU clusters. Infrastructure rather than a retail model API.

title: GMI Cloud
brief: GPU cloud with serverless inference APIs and dedicated endpoints; lists H100 at $2/GPU-hour and H200 at $2.60/GPU-hour.

title: Venice
brief: Private AI chat and API with free entry and paid tiers (Pro $18/mo). Its API carries a zero-data-retention promise.

title: Relace
brief: Coding-focused API (Instant Apply model, code retrieval, embeddings, reranking) rather than general LLM inference. Available via Continue.dev, with a self-host/VPC option.

title: AntSeed
brief: Open market for AI inference with no account or email required and optional TEE-backed providers. That design is not the same as a universal zero-retention promise.

title: Inco
brief: Inference company from the Inco (confidential-computing) team, branding itself 'inference, reimagined for the agentic era.' It open-sourced Splash, a local inference engine claiming 144 tokens/s on an M5 Max with Qwen3.8-27B (integrated into LM Studio), and its earlier DFlash speculative-decoding tech was adopted by SGLang, vLLM, TensorRT-LLM, llama.cpp, plus Meta, NVIDIA, and Xiaomi. The 144 tokens/s figure is a peak vendor-demonstration value, not an independently verified benchmark; the public site is still sparse with no visible pricing or hosted-API details.

title: Kenari
brief: An Indonesian AI cloud and gateway: one API key and one Rupiah wallet behind an OpenAI-compatible endpoint, with per-token prices quoted in Rupiah (e.g. DeepSeek V4 Flash at Rp 2,750 input / Rp 5,500 output per 1M tokens, GLM-5.3-Flash at Rp 2,000/Rp 6,000), top-ups from Rp 1,000, free models, and free BYOK routing through its dashboard. Also bundles one-click app hosting ('Pods' — n8n, OpenClaw, a WhatsApp gateway) and monthly plans from Rp 49rb.

title: InferenceSaver
brief: Unified API and SDK routing requests across 1,000+ models from many providers with automatic fallbacks, best-price optimization, and a real-time observability dashboard. Markets itself as one API for every AI model, advertising per-model 'up to 70% off' rates and 40–80% savings on inference spend. The savings and discount figures are vendor marketing, not independently verified.
caveat: The savings and discount figures are vendor marketing, not independently verified.

title: Nube
brief: Inference API with published per-token pricing. States explicit zero data retention with an upstream no-training clause.

title: Cline Pass
brief: Subscription for Cline's coding agent at $9.99/mo, positioned as 2–5x the quota versus direct API spend. The "5x cheaper than API" phrasing seen in chatter is not verified.

title: Nebius Token Factory
brief: Nebius's pay-per-token hosted inference for open text/vision models (~23 models incl. DeepSeek, Llama, Qwen). New accounts get trial credit; uses separate v1 API credentials.

title: Coral Bricks
brief: High-throughput inference aimed at agents. A forwarded promo code (SUPERINT) covered GLM 5.2 and Kimi K3.

title: Fast Inference
brief: Gateway for AI models and coding agents with provider failover. $9/mo gives $10 gateway credit, $49/mo gives $60, then pay-as-you-go at direct rates.

title: Entrim
brief: $10 in credits plus pay-as-you-go inference. Processes prompts and outputs in RAM only and does not train on them.

title: Merge Gateway
brief: Multi-provider gateway. A Discord-shared "75% off DeepSeek V4 Flash through September 30" promo was not corroborated on its site.

title: sference
brief: Managed inference for open models on European GPUs. Public evidence is snippet-based; details unverified.
caveat: Public evidence is snippet-based; details unverified.

title: Unifically
brief: Pay-per-use multi-model API (no subscription) with a $0.20 free balance and per-generation pricing, e.g. $0.03 per image. The sharer called it "sus" — treat vendor claims cautiously.

title: Reflex
brief: Post-trained Kimi K3 served with 6x context at a claimed 490 tokens/sec. Performance claims come from the provider's own page.

title: OpenModels
brief: Credit-subscription marketplace spanning 333 models, 100+ live routes, and 24+ providers: plans from $5/mo ($6 credits) to $99/mo ($110 credits), with credits that never expire and roll over. Every plan unlocks every model route; usage is billed per token based on the selected provider route, and one-time top-ups accept USDC.

title: OpenRouter
brief: Multi-provider model gateway charging a 5.5% fee, with 50 free requests/day. Shared via its GLM 5.3 provider/pricing page.

title: TensorX
brief: EU-hosted pay-as-you-go inference whose pricing page states verbatim: "all inference is zero data retention."

title: AI Router
brief: Swiss-hosted inference API ("All of AI. One API. Made in Switzerland") with GDPR compliance and data hosted in Switzerland. Flat CHF 39/mo unlimited under a fair-use policy; OpenAI-compatible at api.airouter.ch/v1.

title: B.AI
brief: Unified LLM API at api.b.ai/v1 where one key speaks three protocols — OpenAI Chat Completions, OpenAI Responses, and Anthropic Messages — with docs at docs.b.ai. It gained traction for generous free models (DeepSeek-V4-Flash, Tencent HY3, MiMo-V2.5, GLM-5.3-Flash), though its promotions page moved free offers to limited-time 10%-of-reference discounts on 16 Sep 2026, leaving only a 300,000-credit (~$0.30, 30-day) referral gift; login is via Web3 wallet or Google. Homepage details are unverified beyond third-party reviews from mid-Sep 2026, so confirm current pricing on the site itself.
caveat: Homepage details are unverified beyond third-party reviews from mid-Sep 2026, so confirm current pricing on the site itself.

title: OrcaRouter
brief: Zero-markup BYOK router with an open-source self-hostable Lite (MIT); the hosted plan includes free credits. Pass-through per-token pricing, e.g. DeepSeek V4 Flash $0.15/$0.29 per 1M in/out.

title: OpenFerence
brief: Inference API at openference.ai; public evidence is snippet-based only. A Discord claim that its GLM 5.2 "is not even real" is unverified.
caveat: A Discord claim that its GLM 5.2 "is not even real" is unverified.

title: wafer
brief: Inference provider, with DeepSeek V4 Flash mentioned on it in later chatter. Surfaced via an X post from @wafer_ai.

title: Fireworks AI
brief: Serverless inference from $0.10/1M tokens (under 4B params), $1 free starter credit, 50% off batch. 100–400+ open models with an OpenAI-compatible API, FireAttention engine, LoRA/RFT fine-tuning and dedicated GPUs.

title: RunInfra
brief: Inference provider; its DeepSeek V4 Flash $0.13/M input price was corroborated. A "1.8¢/M blended" figure seen in chatter is not a list price.

title: Freebuff
brief: Free, ad-supported coding agent (CLI, desktop, web, cloud, chat) powered by open models like DeepSeek V4 Pro/Flash and MiniMax M3. Explicit no-training stance — it doesn't share data with third parties that would train on it.

title: GripHubRouter
brief: A pay-as-you-go multi-model router aimed at Indonesian developers: 47 models from 12 vendors behind one OpenAI-compatible endpoint, with credits at Rp 300 each, top-ups from Rp 15,000 via QRIS, and no subscription or foreign card required. A one-click installer wires it into VS Code, Claude Code, OpenCode, GitHub Copilot, and Hermes Agent, and a live status widget shows gateway response times.

title: Melious
brief: EU-hosted pay-as-you-go inference; the sharer cited ~240 tok/s on DeepSeek V4 Flash. States it does not train on user data.

title: SiliconFlow
brief: One OpenAI-compatible API for open and commercial LLMs with serverless pay-as-you-go and dedicated endpoints. Homepage claim: "No data stored, ever."

title: CheaperInference
brief: Pay-as-you-go inference with published example rates. Prompt and response bodies are not logged, with zero data retention on supported routes.

title: Novita
brief: AI-native cloud combining serverless model APIs (200+ models through one API, billed per token) with dedicated private endpoints, secure isolated agent sandboxes, and GPU cloud (on-demand instances, serverless GPU, bare metal). One platform for the full AI stack — model APIs, GPUs, and agent runtimes — backed by testimonials from Hugging Face, Kilo Code, and Fish Audio. Its 'up to 50% less than major cloud providers' claim is vendor-reported and not independently verified.
caveat: Its 'up to 50% less than major cloud providers' claim is vendor-reported and not independently verified.

title: Command Code
brief: GOAT plan — $10/mo for $70 in credits (limits $14/5h, $35/week, $70/month) across 30+ open and closed models. No zero-retention statement found.

title: DeepSeek
brief: DeepSeek's official API pricing: pay-as-you-go with 50% off-peak discounts (Flash $0.15/$0.60, Pro $0.66/$1.98 per 1M in/out on cache miss; peak is 2x). The $0.13/$0.30 figures seen in Discord are stale.

title: YOLO Auto
brief: Unlimited-token API plans, currently $19/$39 — the Discord-era $6/mo claim is superseded. Shared as an unlimited Qwen3.6-35B API.

title: Claudin.io

title: Antidoom (Liquid AI blog)
brief: Liquid AI's method for killing the repetitive 'doom loops' that plague small reasoning models: Final Token Preference Optimization trains the model to prefer coherent alternatives at the exact token where a loop begins, leaving the rest of the distribution untouched. On an early LFM2.5-2.6B checkpoint it cut loop rates from 10.2% to 1.4%, and on Qwen3.5-4B from 22.9% to 1% under greedy sampling — with the generation, detection, and training code open-sourced. Results are vendor-reported on vendor checkpoints and not independently verified.
caveat: Results are vendor-reported on vendor checkpoints and not independently verified.

title: Kimi K3 on MI355X (Wafer blog)
brief: Wafer benchmarked Moonshot's 2.8T-parameter Kimi K3 on AMD's MI355X (288GB VRAM per GPU): 952 tok/s/node aggregate and 118 tok/s single-stream — over 3.8× the per-node throughput of a 2-node B200 deployment. With the MI355X ~2.4× cheaper per GPU than NVIDIA's B300, it wins decisively on performance per dollar; the post also details real ROCm fixes, including speculative decode via RadixArk's DSpark draft and zero-padding heads to unlock the AITER MLA prefill kernel. All throughput figures are vendor-reported and not independently verified.
caveat: All throughput figures are vendor-reported and not independently verified.
